solve.reasoning: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is given by P = 4T/r, where r is the radius of curvature. A hemispherical bubble at end 1 has radius r, so its excess pressure is 4T/r. A sub-hemispherical bubble at end 2 has a radius of curvature R < r (since it is smaller than a hemisphere). Therefore, the excess pressure at end 2 is 4T/R, which is greater than 4T/r. When the valve opens, air flows from the region of higher pressure to the region of lower pressure. Thus, air flows from end 2 to end 1, causing the bubble at end 1 to grow in size.
